## Current Task402 disposition

This remains an open, repository-maintainer-owned reliability follow-up under the existing [CR-212-04 merits-based decision](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/pull/212#issuecomment-5896646906). It is not claimed complete by removal of the old inline commands or by successful normal setup.

At accepted PS main `48f4d8a36c8faceee12afac78aaecea0d176125d`, the old sites below have been replaced or deleted. The reachable ordinary download is now in `.github/workflows/Initialize-CiToolchain.ps1`. It has `--connect-timeout 20`, `--max-time 180` and `--retry 2`, but no total retry-duration option. The actual Terraform counterpart at `06ad4f7c9b6847028cafdacf1ae55128d0f2d56c` has the same transfer/retry flags. The separate Copilot setup already has `--retry-max-time 300`. Existing helper tests cover download failure and wrong bytes; they do not prove ordinary Retry-After exhaustion behavior.

A bounded local curl8.5.0 test used a loopback HTTP503 response with Retry-After5. With connection/transfer limits1second and retry2, the process was still sleeping when the harness stopped it at2.005seconds; this is an intentionally stopped run, not a pass. When this follow-up starts, recheck the current actual download consumers and the shared Terraform initializer. Use the full decision process to choose a useful retry/overall failure budget and coupled negative tests. Preserve archive origin, digest-before-execution, locked runtime selection and native failure handling. The historical three-site inventory below records the finding's origin. It is not the current repair locator.

open_issues.title: Require immutable event revisions as workflow acquisition sources
open_issues.body:
## Problem

The current YAML guide requires a privileged workflow to verify the fetched commit after acquisition. It does not require an immutable event revision as the acquisition source.

A run can fetch `github.ref` after another event moves that ref. The later comparison with `github.sha` detects the mismatch but cannot recover the event commit. The run then fails although the immutable event commit remains valid and retrievable.

## Deferral rationale and trigger

PR #174 did not receive authorization for another protected guide edit. Start this work only after a maintainer explicitly authorizes `.github/instructions/yaml.instructions.md` and the exact rule scope in a new implementation task.

This issue does not provide that authorization. It does not start implementation.

## Affected scope

The future rule applies to GitHub Actions jobs that claim to validate one immutable event commit. It includes privileged `pull_request_target` jobs and similar jobs that fetch or check out Git data.

Keep least privilege, non-forcing fetches, bounded acquisition, and exact post-acquisition commit verification. Do not change the completed workflow repair through this guide task.

## Origin and implemented workflow

- Candidate PR: https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/pull/174
- Origin thread: https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/pull/174#discussion_r3834358343
- Disposition reply: https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/pull/174#discussion_r3834638076
- Implemented workflow commit: `00d380586bb728544bad921f1ab809d49646a89b`
- Implemented workflow tree: `9dbea0305812650d4143df6f8cba8f195881fc12`
- Implemented workflow path: `.github/workflows/devcontainer-ci.yml`

PR #174 already fixes the workflow at the recorded commit and tree. This issue tracks only future guide work.

## Examples

Compliant acquisition uses the immutable event revision as the fetch source.

```yaml
env:
  EXPECTED_REVISION: ${{ github.sha }}
```

```sh
git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin \
  "${EXPECTED_REVISION}:refs/remotes/event/target"
actual_revision="$(git rev-parse --verify 'refs/remotes/event/target^{commit}')"
test "$actual_revision" = "$EXPECTED_REVISION"
```

Noncompliant acquisition resolves a mutable ref first and compares the result later.

```yaml
env:
  EXPECTED_REF: ${{ github.ref }}
  EXPECTED_REVISION: ${{ github.sha }}
```

```sh
git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin \
  "${EXPECTED_REF}:refs/remotes/event/target"
actual_revision="$(git rev-parse --verify 'refs/remotes/event/target^{commit}')"
test "$actual_revision" = "$EXPECTED_REVISION"
```

The final comparison is necessary, but it is insufficient when acquisition resolves a mutable ref. It detects the race after acquisition instead of preventing it.

## Acceptance and validation

- [ ] State that an immutable event revision must be the fetch or checkout source.
- [ ] Prohibit mutable-ref acquisition followed only by expected-revision comparison.
- [ ] Preserve the least-privilege, no-force, bounded-fetch, and exact-commit rules.
- [ ] Include one compliant immutable-revision example and one noncompliant mutable-ref example.
- [ ] Record explicit maintainer authorization before changing `.github/instructions/yaml.instructions.md`.
- [ ] Update the guide version and date as its instructions require.
- [ ] Add a ref-move validation fixture that proves immutable acquisition remains deterministic.
- [ ] Verify `.github/workflows/devcontainer-ci.yml` conforms at the recorded commit and tree.
- [ ] Run repository instruction validation, Markdown validation, front-matter YAML parsing, and two clean full pre-commit passes.
- [ ] Record exact commands, native exits, changed paths, Git objects, bytes, and SHA-256 values.

Do not assign this issue, attach it to a project, create a relationship, or link a branch during creation.

# Artifact generator and verifier: remaining filesystem race and path-identity limitations

## Current disposition

The repository maintainer owns this open residual record. Task379 selects no product repair at this time. Accepted [PR221](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/pull/221) retired the old archive extractor, invocation-context helper, harness and catalog. Their extraction, directory-adoption and two-root alias paths have no remaining consumer. Removal reduces applicability; it does not fix their historical races.

The current `Generate-StyleGuideArtifacts.ps1` and `Test-ExactGitPathSet.ps1` still use paths for some reads, publication and cleanup. Before/after checks do not prove that no transient replacement occurred. The verifier's GUID-named temporary-directory creation and cleanup also have a race surface under a competing-writer threat model. This assessment did not reproduce a supported-caller failure, establish a new untrusted-writer requirement, or prove universal Windows alias/handle identity.

Reassess when a supported current caller reproduces a failure, a deliberate requirement admits concurrent untrusted writers, a concrete usable runtime/API improvement addresses these operations, or a new consumer has materially different authority. A date, version change alone, retired phase name or old test count does not trigger implementation. Start any selected repair with a scoped decision and meaningful tests. Do not recreate deleted helpers merely to close their old findings.

The original findings and measured/unmeasured limits below remain historical evidence. Retired coverage obligations are recorded in [issue156](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/issues/156).

Full validation, options, separate weighted rubrics, scores and selected instructions: [Task379 decisions D92/D93](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/issues/155#issuecomment-5943334454).

## Historical residual record

## Summary

PR #153's fail-closed candidate validator **narrows but does not fully close** a
family of time-of-check/time-of-use (TOCTOU) and path-identity gaps in
`Expand-StyleGuideCandidateArtifact.ps1` and
`Manage-StyleGuideCandidateInvocationContext.ps1`. Each remaining gap has the
same shape: the code proves a path's identity, then acts on it, and a competing
writer acting inside that window — or a Windows alias the canonical spelling
cannot express — can still defeat the proof. Closing any of them requires an
OS-native primitive that portable .NET does not expose and Windows PowerShell
5.1 cannot reach without P/Invoke.

This issue records the residual so it survives PR #153's merge, rather than
living only in that PR's "Known gaps" section and its (now resolved) review
threads.

## The residual gaps

| Gap | Where | What still gets through |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Extraction race | `Expand` extraction loop | One output can land outside trusted storage if a competing writer wins the race between the identity proof and the create; an ancestor swapped inside the loop is not caught by the leaf-only probe. |
| Directory-creation race | invocation-root / candidate creation | An *empty* directory placed at the chosen name inside the race window is still adopted. |
| Windows root separation (alias -> descendant) | Windows identity chain | An alias mapped to a *descendant* of the checkout is not detected; the canonical spelling cannot express link-ness on Windows. |
| Regular-file-proof -> open window | every opening site | The window between the regular-file proof and the open is not closed (mitigated today by the `0700` invocation root). |

## Why it cannot be closed as written

- Closing the races needs **handle-relative creation with no-follow semantics**
  (open the parent by handle, create relative to it, refuse to follow links).
  Portable .NET does not expose this; Windows PowerShell 5.1 needs P/Invoke.
- Windows link/identity detection needs **handle-based identity**
  (`GetFileInformationByHandleEx`), again P/Invoke on 5.1.
- The only actor who can trigger the races is a **competing untrusted writer**,
  which issue #146 lists under **Non-goals**. So this is a scope question as
  well as an implementation one — the same actor and the same non-goal that make
  `PS-P1A-K-04`'s oracle unreachable (#154).

## What bounds the residual today

Containment and root separation still decide *where* a write may land; the
invocation root is `0700`, so a different unprivileged user cannot reach it; and
the manager's evidence pass refuses at cleanup when the candidate directory
holds anything the ownership journal does not describe. The gaps are exploitable
only by the excluded competing-writer actor.

## Reopen / trigger conditions

Revisit when any of these becomes true:

1. The P1A contract (#146) is revised to admit a bounded competing writer (see
   #154), making the behavior both reachable and in scope; or
2. The minimum supported runtime drops Windows PowerShell 5.1, so a portable
   no-follow / handle-relative API can close the window on every supported
   runtime without per-platform P/Invoke; or
3. P1B (#147) or a later phase adopts a P/Invoke helper, at which point these
   gaps should be closed together.

## References

- PR #153 — "Known gaps -> Security-relevant and open" (the four rows above) and
  the reciprocal P1A<->T1A redline.
- Issue #146 — P1A contract, **Non-goals** ("a competing untrusted writer").
- Issue #154 — the same actor/non-goal makes the `PS-P1A-K-04` oracle unreachable.
- Issue #147 — P1B, the natural home for a shared P/Invoke primitive.

## Added residual (PR #153, round 74): journal-corruption rollback leak

A fifth same-session residual belongs to this family, recorded here so it outlives PR #153's merge alongside the four filesystem-TOCTOU gaps above.

**The gap.** In `Expand-StyleGuideCandidateArtifact.ps1`, if a same-session writer corrupts a *pre-existing* ownership-journal record **in place** (the root or download record's `EntryState` / `Path` / `Kind`) after the expansion authenticated the context, the expansion's own rollback (`Remove-StyleGuideCandidateInvocationState`) re-validates the corrupted live context, refuses with `cleanup-context-invalid` and **zero filesystem calls**, and the `0700` owner-only `root+download(+candidate/files)` tree is **retained** on disk.

**How it differs from the four gaps above.** Those need an OS-native no-follow / handle-relative primitive (P/Invoke on 5.1) — genuinely *unclosable* portably. This one *is* closable in-process (round 73 shipped a "deep capture" that removed the tree from an immutable capture instead of the corrupted live journal). But every in-process closure requires an **unauthenticated (or separately authenticated) deletion primitive**, and the round-73 deep-capture form of it was a **P1**: `Remove-StyleGuideCandidateInvocationState` is public, and a dot-sourcing caller with an invalid `Context` and a forged `-DeepCapture` could delete arbitrary files (reproduced). So the deep-capture was **reverted** at `0360fb5`, and this leak is accepted as a bounded residual rather than closed by a mechanism whose attack surface exceeds it.

**What bounds it.** It is **reported** (`Success=$false`, never a false cleanup success); the retained tree stays inside **owner-only `0700`** trusted storage (no containment breach — weaker than the extraction-race gap above); and it is triggerable **only by the excluded competing-writer actor** (#146 Non-goals). The catch that refuses it carries this note in-code.

**Reopen / trigger conditions.** Revisit if: (1) #146 is revised to admit a bounded competing writer (as for #154), making the actor in scope; or (2) a manager-authenticated capture — one that binds the deletion target to manager-issued immutable state — is designed whose added attack surface is justified, at which point the in-process closure becomes worth its cost.

**References:** PR #153 round-74 review threads (P1 [`discussion_r3741097083`](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/pull/153#discussion_r3741097083)); #146 Non-goals (*"a competing untrusted writer"*); the in-code note at the `cleanup-context-invalid` catch in `Expand-StyleGuideCandidateArtifact.ps1`.

## Added residual (PR #153 pre-merge sweep): the harness runs the path, not the authenticated bytes

A sixth same-session residual belongs to this family. I record it here so it outlives PR #153's merge, next to the four filesystem-TOCTOU gaps and the round-74 journal-corruption leak. Until now it lived only in the PR body's "Security-relevant and open" list, with no issue number — unlike its four siblings, which cite this issue.

**The gap.** `Test-Expand-StyleGuideCandidateArtifact.ps1` authenticates each production script (`Expand-StyleGuideCandidateArtifact.ps1`, `Manage-StyleGuideCandidateInvocationContext.ps1`) by its Git blob identity — HEAD tree blob, stage-0 index blob, and no-filter working-object ID — and by its expected version. It proves this **twice**: before it dot-sources the script, and again immediately before it invokes the functions (per #146, "Trusted harness script interface"). It then loads the script **from the same path**. A competing writer that replaces the file bytes in the window between the final proof and the dot-source read makes the harness execute bytes it did not authenticate. This is the harness-side analogue of the production archive gap that Amendment A closed for the ZIP bytes.

**Why it is not fixed now (options considered).** The in-process fix is to read each script once into memory after the proof, re-compute the Git blob hash of those bytes in process, and execute them with `[ScriptBlock]::Create` — binding execution to the authenticated bytes. It is **not taken**, for three reasons:

1. **The actor is out of scope.** Only the competing untrusted writer that #146 lists under **Non-goals** can trigger it. It is the same actor and non-goal that make `PS-P1A-K-04` unreachable (#154) and that bound the rest of this family.
2. **It is test-harness code**, not production. The blast radius is test integrity, not a production-security breach.
3. **The fix has real cost and needs a contract change.** #146 mandates a dot-source from the *path*; executing an in-memory script block deviates from that mandated mechanism and would need an amendment (as Amendment A did for production). An in-memory block also loses `$PSScriptRoot`/`$PSCommandPath` and does **not** honor `#Requires -Version 5.1` — PowerShell applies neither to a `ScriptBlock.Create` block. `FileShare.None` across the window is not an alternative: .NET does not enforce share modes on Unix, which is the exact lesson Amendment A recorded.

This mirrors the round-74 decision on the journal-corruption leak: closable in principle, but the closure's cost/attack-surface exceeds the bounded residual, so it stays documented and tracked here rather than closed.

**What bounds it.** The harness runs in a trusted context (owner/developer or the workflow-inert P1A test run), not on hostile input. The production scripts are own-repo files. The double proof — before load and before invocation — narrows the window. A swap still needs the excluded competing-writer actor with write access to the checkout during the run.

**Reopen / trigger conditions.** Revisit if any becomes true:
1. #146 is revised to admit a bounded competing writer (as for #154/#155), making the actor in scope; or
2. a later phase (P1B, #147) adopts a P/Invoke or in-memory-execution helper whose added surface is justified, at which point the authenticate-then-execute binding becomes worth its cost; or
3. the minimum supported runtime drops Windows PowerShell 5.1, so a portable no-follow/handle-relative primitive can close the window on every supported runtime.

**References.**

## Summary

Replace truncating manual-backup redirections and unguarded destructive state commands with a small, explicit operational workflow:

1. capture a current state snapshot into a protected temporary file;
2. validate the Terraform exit, state format, lineage, serial, and digest;
3. publish the backup to a fresh path without overwrite;
4. verify exact workspace/backend/concurrency identity;
5. preview and review the intended mutation;
6. require an explicit human confirmation bound to that identity;
7. run without force or lock bypass; and
8. verify the result and retain a tested recovery point and procedure.

Prefer declarative Terraform workflows (`removed`/`moved`/`import` blocks, normal plan/apply, provider-version rollback) over manual state mutation whenever they can express the operation.

## Dependencies and order

Implement after:

1. **Make state-version discovery and recovery examples copy-safe with guarded identifiers**; and
2. **Remediate Markdown lint dependency advisories and add npm update governance**.

The state-recovery dependency supplies the canonical protected-destination primitive and exact-block harness. T3 completes before this issue to avoid simultaneous changes to shared generated documentation and the callable Markdown workflow.

Record real blocked-by relationships and exact merge commits.

### Mandatory internal review gates

T4 remains one issue but has two separately approved evidence gates.

**Gate A — nonmutating foundation:** implement and freeze only protected parent/path inspection, state-pull capture/publication, state inspection, difference review, address parsing/resolution, confirmation construction/read, case catalog, and their no-mutation harnesses. Record the reviewed commit/tree, every helper version/blob/SHA-256, exact role-table version, catalogs/results, platform/runtime/tool identities, and an operator plus independent peer approval. Gate A fixtures prove mutation child-call count is zero.

**Gate B — destructive procedures:** may start only from Gate A's exact immutable identities and approvals. Any Gate A code, role, schema, path, limit, confirmation, or evidence change invalidates approval and returns to Gate A. # Retired P1A helpers: historical coverage limitations

## Current disposition

Closed as **not planned** because accepted [PR221](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/pull/221) removed the relevant extractor, invocation-context helper, test harness and catalog. No executable consumer of the old proof-wiring assertion, journal cap or E05 case remains. Retirement is complete; the old tests are not newly passing and the historical filesystem races are not claimed repaired.

Keep the measured, unmeasured and unreachable coverage below as history. Current generator/verifier risks and their repository-maintainer owner are recorded in [issue155](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/issues/155). That current implementation does not inherit old ACL, non-GNU stat or E05 coverage.

Add a new coverage task only when a specific supported consumer needs the property, a current failure is reproduced, or a changed runtime/security requirement makes a particular branch relevant. Do not recreate the old helper or catalog solely to satisfy an obsolete test obligation. No product code changed for this disposition.

Full validation, options, separate weighted rubrics, scores and selected instructions: [Task379 decisions D92/D93](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/issues/155#issuecomment-5943334454).

## Historical residual record

## Summary

PR #153 deliberately records several hardening steps as *recommended rather than
taken*, and several validation-coverage caveats where a property holds on the
runtimes exercised but has not been measured elsewhere. None blocks the PR; all
are honest residuals that would otherwise be lost when #153 merges. This issue
tracks them so the decision to pick them up later is rediscoverable.

## Recommended-not-taken hardening

| Item | Current state | Recommended step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Regular-file-proof wiring | Round 59 pins the three call sites by **count** (`scriptBlockAssertOrdinaryFileProofWired`). A decoy invocation elsewhere could hold the count at three while the post-extraction call was removed. | Convert to a **positional / dataflow** assertion so a fourth opening site is inexpressible, not merely counted. Deferred because a wide AST rule over `open` is exactly the surface this loop kept getting wrong; the realistic regression is a dropped call, which the count catches. |
| Journal-record cap coverage | The record-count cap has no catalog row; `PS-P1A-C-09` proves the identical property for a forged `ContentLength`. | Add a catalog row (or dedicated harness assertion) that drives the record-count cap directly. |

## Validation coverage not reachable on the tested runtimes

Each holds on the runtimes actually run (Windows PowerShell 5.1 / Windows,
PowerShell 7.6.4 / Windows and Ubuntu) but has an unmeasured edge:

- **Windows ACL negative branch** — the owner-only ACL applied at context
  creation has executed (contexts were created on both Windows runtimes), but no
  run has exercised a host where the ACL *cannot* be applied, so the **refusal
  path is reasoned, not observed**.
- **Domain-joined host with inherited ACEs** — the canonical-spelling identity
  chain and the sentinel probe's ACL behavior held across 115 cases on each
  Windows runtime, but not on a domain-joined host with inherited ACEs.
- **Non-GNU coreutils** — the regular-file proof parses GNU-style `%f`; only GNU
  coreutils 9.4 has been measured (BusyBox / BSD `stat` differ).
- **Non-Linux filtered-absence pattern matching** — the filtered absence proofs
  inherit the platform's pattern-matching rules; only Linux has been measured.
- **`PS-P1A-E-05`** cannot prove the provider check *specifically* ran, and the
  guard checks do not prove the guard's return value is what production carries
  forward.

## Not in scope here

The race-dependent gaps (extraction race, directory-creation race, Windows
alias-to-descendant, regular-file-proof -> open window) are tracked separately in
Issue #155 — they need the competing-writer actor #146 excludes. The `PS-P1A-K-04`
oracle conflict is #154.

## Reopen / trigger conditions

Pick up opportunistically during P1B (#147) or the next time these files are
edited; or when CI gains a domain-joined Windows runner or a non-GNU-coreutils
runner that would let the unmeasured edges be exercised deterministically.

## References

- PR #153 — "Known gaps -> Coverage and correctness" and the "Flagged
  deviations" recommended-not-taken notes (regular-file-proof wiring,
  journal-record cap).
- Issue #146 — P1A contract and Non-goals.
- Issues #147 (P1B), #154 (`PS-P1A-K-04` oracle), #155 (the race family).
